title: multi-tenant-noisyneighbor-throttle-log
content:
High-level: observed ~30-50% sustained throughput drop on a small subset of hosts servicing mixed-tenant traffic. Symptoms appeared ~2024-03-19 03:40 UTC and persisted intermittently for ~8 hours. Rooty suspicion: a noisy tenant created steady small microbatches that caused continuous prefill + cache churn + GPU memory pressure which escalated the cbatch window and triggered per-request tail latency that reduced effective throughput. But logs show odd backpressure points and some allocator resets.

Quick reproduction steps used locally:
1) stress-client to mimic noisy tenant: ./tools/stress-client --host host:8080 --concurrency 64 --payload-size 700 --qps 200 --seed 42
2) baseline client (control) for normal tenant: wrk -t8 -c128 -d60s http://host:8080/generate
3) monitor: kubectl top pod -n serving --selector app=runtime; nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -l 1; curl http://host:9090/metrics | grep cbatch

Commands run on impacted node (snips):
- docker ps | grep runtime
  3a4f9b9 runtime:latest   "/bin/runtime --config ..."   12 hours ago
- kubectl describe pod runtime-xyz -n serving
  Events:
    Warning  BackOff  2m (x5 over 10m) kubelet back-off restarting failed container

Telemetry/log snippets (redacted):
- allocator: evicting slab id=0x7f8 size=45MB free=12MB -> reason=high-watermark
- cbatch: window-size=14 -> window-growth-triggered=user-pacing
- prefill: kv_cache_miss=0.87 rate=120/s
- gpu: oom_kill_count=0 but peak_alloc=90% mem_total=24GB mem_free=2.3GB
- http: 503 upstream-overloaded for request_id=abc123 (latency spike 980ms)

Experiments tried (results):
A) Pin noisy tenant to its own node pool (taint + toleration) — immediate recovery on victim hosts. Throughput back to baseline in 2 minutes. Suggests cross-tenant interference.
B) Disabled prefix-caching for runtime on one host (env PREFILL_CACHE=false) — small improvement (10%) but not full. Indicates cache churn part of problem.
C) Lowered cbatch max-window from 20 -> 8 via config toggle — helped tail latency but increased GPU idle (lower throughput). Tradeoff obvious.
D) Applied a token rate limiter on per-tenant scheduler (soft limit) — mitigated but customer-facing; still exploring fairer throttling.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Noisy tenant small-batch pattern forces frequent KV-cache invalidation and frequent prefill requests that create many short-lived allocations in runtime slab allocator -> fragmentation and transient free pressure -> cbatch growth and higher per-token overhead.
2) Scheduling policy uses a single global backpressure signal; when memory pressure occurs on one node, it widens cbatch windows globally for that node leading to underutilization for other tenants on same host.
3) GPU memory accounting (driver/containers) underreports transient spikes, so OOMs are avoided with thrashing instead (lots of allocations freed/allocated) which is worse for throughput than occasional OOM-kills.
4) Some tenant-specific client behavior (many concurrent streams with small prompt sizes) interacts poorly with the continuous-batcher's window heuristics causing oscillation.

Interesting log anomaly to follow-up:
- At 2024-03-19T04:22:11Z: "cbatch: flush-request window=9 reason=internal-timer (expected 3)" — internal timer triggered unusually late; need to correlate with system clock skew / GC pause / scheduler hitch.
- At 2024-03-19T05:03:40Z: repeated: "slab: free-list corruption detected, repairing" — we haven't triggered this before; might be a bug in allocator under high churn.

Immediate mitigation checklist (what I did + notes):
- Isolate noisy tenant via node affinity (applied) -> good stopgap
- Add per-tenant request rate limiter (deployed with soft limits) -> reduced tail but not perfect
- Raise prefill thread pool lower bound to avoid long lat spikes (tuned on 3 hosts) -> slightly better
- Hotfix: revert allocator change from last deploy (rolled back) -> no change (so not the recent allocator diff)

Data to collect for next steps (required):
- Full nvidia-smi top + driver logs for 24h window on impacted host
- Heap/allocator histograms (malloc free high-water marks) correlated with cbatch window size (attach pprof if possible)
- Client traces from noisy tenant (timestamps, payload sizes, inter-arrival distribution)
- System-level scheduling events (dmesg, kubelet events) to see if CPU steal/HZ jitter correlated

Proposed long term fixes / design thoughts:
- Introduce per-tenant soft quotas at scheduler layer that bound active prefill / kv-cache working set.
- Improve allocator to coalesce small frees and avoid fragmentation hotspots when churn is high (or use jemalloc tuned for small object churn).
- Make cbatch window growth more local: window decisions should consider tenant affinity and per-queue backpressure rather than host-global signals.
- Add a "microbatch smoothing" layer: collapse many small concurrent requests from same tenant into synthetic grouping before hitting runtime.
- Better telemetry: expose per-tenant kv_cache_miss, per-tenant prefill rate, and per-host slab fragmentation metric.

Notes / to-dos for me:
- Create a minimal reproducer that simulates noisy tenant with 4 concurrent streams each producing small payloads at 8–12 qps. Capture allocator/gpu metrics. (target: by 2024-04-05)
- Open a follow-up GH issue for slab repair message + allocator stack trace (need core dump) -> assign to @Liam
- Discuss with product: acceptable per-tenant soft limits for hosted customers (session with Sofia)
- Draft quick runbook for oncall: steps to isolate noisy tenant and restore throughput (short doc)

Misc commands & snippets to run next time:
- kubectl exec -it runtime-xyz -n serving -- sh -c "pprof --text /metrics/alloc 1m > /tmp/alloc.txt"
- python tools/latency-probe.py --target host:8080 --streams 8 --payload small --duration 300 --out=./trace.json
- while true; do curl -s http://host:9090/metrics | egrep 'cbatch|kv_cache|slab' >> /tmp/host-metrics.log; sleep 2; done &

End notes: This one felt like an emergent multi-tenant scheduling problem more than a single regression. Isolation fixed quickly which is a strong signal. Next milestone: reproduce deterministically and tighten the cbatch-localization logic (or add tenant-aware heuristics).
